_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `crustify-oracle <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through crustify.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

types.name: git_annotated_commit

Internal inspection shows the discriminant selects two ownership variants: real commits own commit/tree and duplicated strings; virtual commits own index and the parents buffer. Pointer members are nullable across the union-like variants and all are released by git_annotated_commit_free.

types.name: git_blob
types._comment_agent: The data union is discriminated by raw: either an owned reference-counted ODB object or a borrowed immutable byte buffer.

types.name: git_branch_iterator
types._comment_agent: Public opaque iterator. Its allocation is uniquely owned and released by git_branch_iterator_free; no fields are published.

types.name: git_branch_t
types._comment_agent: Closed public branch-kind enum with LOCAL and REMOTE values plus the ALL bitwise filter value; it has no pointer or lifecycle fields.

types.name: git_buf
types._comment_agent: Review wave: refined git_buf.ptr with the runtime owned/borrowed witness libgit2 itself uses, so a wrapper can decide writability and detachability from the header alone.

ptr.note: Counted mutable byte buffer. The owned-vs-not gate is decidable from the header: git_buf_fromstr copies git_str::asize into `reserved`, and git_str_is_allocated is `ptr != NULL && asize > 0`, so an owned allocation always has `reserved > size` (a git_str keeps room for the trailing NUL). Two non-owned representations record `reserved == 0`: NULL (GIT_BUF_INIT), and the shared static git_str__initstr sentinel that git_buf_dispose/git_buf_sanitize install for an empty buffer. git_buf_dispose gates on `ptr != git_str__initstr` and frees with git__free; it resets to the sentinel, never to NULL. Corner case: git_str_attach_notowned yields asize==0 with a non-null ptr and size>0 (bytes owned elsewhere, possibly read-only - git_str_try_grow refuses it as 'a borrowed buffer'); git_buf_fromstr would forward that shape, so writes and detachment must require `reserved > size` rather than a non-null pointer. The size excludes the guaranteed trailing NUL but interior NUL bytes are allowed, so this is an array rather than a string.

types.name: git_cached_obj
types._comment_agent: git_cached_obj is the common prefix of git_object and git_odb_object. Its refcount field is atomically incremented/decremented by git_cached_obj_incref/decref; the remaining fields are initialized before cache publication and contain no pointers.

types.name: git_cert

types.name: git_cert_hostkey
types._comment_agent: hostkey is a transient length-delimited byte run borrowed from libssh2 for the synchronous certificate callback. It is meaningful and non-null only with the RAW availability bit; a zero-initialized hostkey record can otherwise hold null.

types.name: git_cert_x509

types.name: git_clone_local_t
types._comment_agent: Closed public C enum with four scalar values and no ownership-bearing fields.

types.name: git_clone_options

types.name: git_commit
types._comment_agent: The public API keeps git_commit opaque. Internally, its reference-counted git_object base ultimately disposes all pointer fields: signatures and strings are individually owned, and parent_ids owns a resizable git_oid buffer. Several members are null during quick/partial parsing, message_encoding and body are optional, and summary/body are populated lazily.

Owned git_signature storage allocated and filled by commit_parse, then released by git_signature_free; null is tolerated during failed partial construction.
Optional encoding-header copy allocated by parsing, owned by the commit, and released by git__free.

types.name: git_config
types._comment_agent: git_config is refcounted through rc: git_config_new initializes one count, repository storage increments it, and git_config_free decrements it before releasing the object.

types.name: git_config_backend_entry
types._comment_agent: git_config_backend_entry embeds git_config_entry as its first member and installs a required static finalizer callback. Ownership is released by dispatching that callback, directly or through git_config_entry_free. Reviewed 2026-08-25: config_file, config_mem and config_list all install git_config_list_entry_free, which drops one reference on the owning git_config_list rather than freeing the entry allocation, so an owning wrapper models a claim on the entry.

ptr.note: Every fully constructed backend entry installs a static concrete finalizer. git_config_entry_free casts the embedded base entry back to git_config_backend_entry and invokes this callback unconditionally. It releases the caller's claim rather than necessarily freeing the entry: config_file, config_mem and config_list all install git_config_list_entry_free, which drops one reference on the git_config_list the entry is embedded in.

types.name: git_config_entry
types._comment_agent: git_config_entry is the public prefix of a dynamically finalized git_config_backend_entry. Its four const char pointers are owned collectively by the concrete backend entry (direct allocations or storage held by its retained config-list); git_config_entry_free invokes the concrete finalizer. The strings remain live for the entry owner's lifetime and are read-only through the published API.

Required normalized NUL-terminated name, retained by the concrete backend entry and released indirectly by its finalizer.
Optional interned NUL-terminated origin path held by the retained config-list and released indirectly by the entry finalizer.
Optional literal NUL-terminated value; valueless configuration entries use NULL. Storage is released indirectly by the concrete entry finalizer.

types.name: git_config_iterator
types._comment_agent: Every fully constructed config iterator is a polymorphic base header whose required static next/free callbacks advance or release its concrete allocation. Internal iterators leave backend null and flags zero after calloc; the sys API permits custom iterators to borrow an originating mutable backend through backend.

Required static synchronous callback installed by every completed iterator; it mutates iterator state and returns a backend entry borrowed until the next advance or iterator destruction.

types.name: git_credential
types._comment_agent: git_credential is a polymorphic public base header. Every fully constructed credential installs a non-null immutable finalizer callback with static code lifetime; the callback frees the concrete allocation and any secret-bearing fields. credtype is a by-value tag holding exactly one published GIT_CREDENTIAL_* kind: every constructor assigns a single constant, and every consumer either switches on the exact value or tests it as one bit against an allowed-types mask, so an empty or combined value is a malformed header rather than a multi-kind credential.

ptr.note: Required concrete finalizer callback installed by every successful credential constructor. The code pointer is static and git_credential_free invokes it exactly once for an owned credential.

types.name: git_describe_format_options
types._comment_agent: Public format options are caller-owned by value and have no lifecycle operation. dirty_suffix is an optional borrowed const C string read synchronously by git_describe__format.

ptr.note: The options struct only borrows this optional NUL-terminated suffix. git_describe__format copies the options by value and reads the string during the formatting call; no path stores, mutates, clones, or frees it. The caller must keep the suffix alive while the options may be used.

types.name: git_describe_options
types._comment_agent: The options struct owns no pointee storage. pattern is an optional borrowed input string whose caller must keep it valid through each describe operation.

ptr.note: Optional caller-owned NUL-terminated match pattern; libgit2 only reads it during describe calls and neither stores a copy nor frees it.

types.name: git_describe_result
types._comment_agent: A describe result owns its optional name/tag variant and borrows its repository. Its public destructor releases the owned variant and result storage but not the repository.

ptr.note: Deep-duplicated exact-match commit_name owned by the result; formatting may lazily populate its tag, and result_free releases its tag, path, and allocation.
Borrowed from the repository owning the input object (or passed to workdir); format uses it but result_free does not release it, so the repository must outlive result use.
Deep-duplicated possible_tag owned by the result; formatting may mutate the nested commit_name, and result_free releases the complete nested allocation.

types.name: git_diff
types._comment_agent: git_diff is publicly opaque but internally refcounted. Its repository slot is a nullable non-owning pointer (parsed diffs leave it null; generated diffs retain a repository borrow). All callback slots are non-owning addresses of static libgit2 functions and are initialized for every fully constructed generated or parsed diff.

Initialized to the generated- or parsed-diff static destructor before publication.
Initialized to the generated- or parsed-diff static patch factory before publication.
Initialized to a static case-sensitive or case-insensitive prefix routine.
Generated diffs borrow their repository and use it for later diff/patch operations; parsed diffs store null. The diff destructor does not release the repository.
Initialized to a static libgit2 comparison routine for every fully constructed diff.
Initialized to a static libgit2 comparison routine for every fully constructed diff.

types.name: git_diff_binary_file
types._comment_agent: The data member is a nullable counted byte allocation. Generation and parsing allocate it through libgit2's configured allocator, and the enclosing patch (or the temporary callback producer) releases it with git__free. Callback consumers borrow the complete git_diff_binary_file and only read its bytes.

types.name: git_diff_file
types._comment_agent: The path is a nullable borrowed NUL-terminated string. Generated diffs point into their owning diff pool; parsed patches point into allocations owned by the enclosing patch, sometimes at an interior offset. The git_diff_file header never independently releases the path.

ptr.note: Borrows a NUL-terminated path kept alive by the enclosing diff or patch. It may be null for an absent/partially initialized side and can point into another owning allocation.

types.name: git_diff_find_options
types._comment_agent: git_diff_find_options is a by-value, non-owning public options record. A custom metric is optional and synchronously borrowed: normalize_find_opts shallow-copies it, invokes its callbacks during git_diff_find_similar, and frees only an internally allocated default metric when the caller supplied none.

ptr.note: Optional custom callback table borrowed by the options value. The table is shallow-copied into normalized stack options, read synchronously, never retained or freed, and must remain live while options using it are passed to libgit2.

types.name: git_diff_format_email_options
types._comment_agent: All four pointers are non-owning inputs. The default initializer stores NULL in each slot; git_diff_format_email requires id, author and summary at call time while body remains optional. The pointed-to values are only read synchronously and are never retained or released by this options value.

ptr.note: Borrowed signature; default NULL, required by git_diff_format_email.
Optional borrowed NUL-terminated commit body.
Borrowed object ID; default NULL, required by git_diff_format_email.
Borrowed NUL-terminated summary; default NULL, required by git_diff_format_email.

types.name: git_diff_line
types._comment_agent: Review wave correction: borrowed.lifetime was recorded as 'self' (the enclosing git_diff_line). No borrowing path stores the bytes inside the line record; every one of them points into another object's storage (generated patch file content, print buffer, or caller buffer), so the field-oriented source is 'other'. The owned path (parsed patches) is unchanged and is what patch_parsed__free releases. Verified against src/libgit2/patch_parse.c:659,701,1154-1156, src/libgit2/diff_xdiff.c:67-80, src/libgit2/diff_print.c:677 and src/libgit2/apply.c:46-55.

ptr.note: Counted, non-NUL-terminated bytes; content_len is the byte count and the pointer is never written through. Runtime-conditional ownership. Owned path: patch_parse.c stores git__strndup results (parse_hunk_body, parse_hunk_body_line) and patch_parsed__free releases each line->content. Borrowed path: the storage always belongs to some OTHER object, never to the enclosing git_diff_line -- diff_xdiff.c's diff_update_lines points at the xdiff mmbuffer backed by the generated patch's loaded ofile/nfile content, diff_print.c's diff_print_patch_file_binary points at the print info's git_str buffer, and apply.c's patch_line_init points at the caller's input buffer. Public observations therefore bind the bytes to the containing patch or to the callback invocation, not to the line record itself. Zero-initialized and empty construction paths permit NULL with length zero.

types.name: git_diff_options
types._comment_agent: git_diff_options is an inline non-owning configuration header. Callback code, callback state, prefixes, and the by-value pathspec view remain caller-owned; libgit2 copies data needed by a constructed diff.

Optional function pointer copied with the options and invoked synchronously; code storage is never owned or mutated.
Optional caller-owned NUL string; diff construction copies it into the diff pool before retaining the normalized option view.
Opaque application state borrowed by the options and passed synchronously to notify/progress callbacks; never freed by the options or diff machinery.
Optional function pointer copied with the options and invoked synchronously; code storage is never owned or mutated.

types.name: git_diff_similarity_metric
types._comment_agent: A metric is a borrowed callback table. payload is an opaque application cookie passed unchanged to every callback; signatures returned by file_signature/buffer_signature are owned by that callback protocol and later released through free_signature, not by the metric struct itself. A valid installed metric supplies all four callbacks. Reviewed 2026-08-25: a signature token transfers to the caller only when its producing callback returns zero; similarity_sig leaves a token published alongside a failure to the callback.

Required code pointer; creates an owned opaque signature token from a borrowed file/path input. The token transfers to the caller on a zero return only: similarity_sig propagates a nonzero status and never releases the slot, and git_diff_find_similar__hashsig_for_file frees its own partial signature without writing the output.
Required code pointer; releases signature tokens using the paired payload.
Opaque borrowed callback cookie, passed through unchanged; callbacks may mutate its referent.
Required code pointer in every valid installed metric.

types.name: git_diff_stats
types._comment_agent: The public type is opaque. Its successful constructor owns one refcounted git_diff handle and one files_changed-length statistics buffer; its public destructor releases both before freeing the header.

ptr.note: git_diff_get_stats stores a non-null git_diff, increments its reference count, and git_diff_stats_free releases that owned count with git_diff_free.

git_diff_get_stats allocates a mutable diff_file_stats array whose element count is files_changed; construction fails if allocation returns null, and git_diff_stats_free releases the buffer with git__free.

types.name: git_email_create_options
types._comment_agent: The public options record owns no pointer storage. subject_prefix is an optional immutable C string borrowed from the caller.

ptr.note: Optional caller-owned NUL-terminated prefix; email formatting only reads it while consuming the options.

types.name: git_error
types._comment_agent: git_error itself has no unconditional lifecycle contract: git_error_last returns libgit2-managed TLS/static storage, while internal git_error_save may allocate a separately freed snapshot. The message field therefore has runtime-conditional owned/borrowed string storage.

ptr.note: Runtime-conditional storage: git_error_save duplicates and owns the NUL-terminated message, the TLS error borrows its containing threadstate's git_str buffer, and static sentinel errors borrow string literals. git_error_free releases only saved non-static objects. Public git_error_last exposes a const borrowed view. NULL is accepted by set_error/restore and free, though ordinary published errors use non-null messages.

types.name: git_fetch_negotiation
types._comment_agent: git_fetch_negotiation has no whole-value destructor. refs is a borrowed pointer container; shallow_roots is a temporary owned counted buffer whose enclosing fetch path explicitly releases it.

Counted git_oid allocation installed by git_repository__shallow_roots, owned temporarily by the negotiation state, read synchronously by the transport and freed with git__free after negotiate_fetch returns; NULL is valid at length zero.

types.name: git_index
types._comment_agent: git_index is publicly opaque but internally refcounted. tree points into the sibling tree_pool arena; comparator slots always borrow static functions; index_file_path owns an optional strdup allocation.

types.name: git_index_conflict_iterator
types._comment_agent: The conflict iterator exclusively owns only its allocation and borrows the external index stored in `index`.

ptr.note: The constructor stores its required index argument without retaining it; iteration reads and may sort the index entries, and the public contract forbids modification while iterating, so the index must outlive the iterator.

types.name: git_index_entry
types._comment_agent: Inspected all path field touchers and index_entry_create/dup/free. The pointer's concrete backing differs between caller-built input values and index-owned returned entries, so the uniform public field contract is a nullable immutable borrowed C string whose actual keeper must outlive every use of the enclosing entry.

Entries stored by an index instead point into trailing storage in entry_internal and remain valid only with that containing entry/index. The field never independently owns or frees the string; null is a valid zero-initialized pre-construction state.

types.name: git_indexer
types._comment_agent: The public API treats git_indexer as opaque. Its retained ODB and callback state are borrowed, while its internal pack singleton is owned and released by git_indexer_free.

ptr.note: Copied from git_indexer_options without an up-ref and never released by git_indexer_free; callers keep the ODB alive through the indexer's use. Read operations receive the non-const ODB handle and may mutate its internal state.

git_packfile_alloc initializes this owned singleton; construction begins with NULL and git_indexer_free releases a successfully constructed pack with git_packfile_free. Indexing mutates the pack and mapped-window state.
Optional callback copied from the options and invoked but never freed or modified; its validity must cover indexer operations and is coupled to progress_payload.
Opaque optional application payload copied from the options and passed to progress_cb without transfer or release; the callback may mutate the pointee and the caller must keep it alive.

types.name: git_indexer_options
types._comment_agent: git_indexer_options owns no pointer field. git_indexer_new copies odb and the callback pair without retaining or releasing them, so their external lifetimes extend through the constructed indexer.

Optional function pointer copied into the indexer and invoked later; code has static lifetime while its paired payload is externally borrowed.
Optional type-erased callback state copied into the indexer and passed back on later progress notifications; the callback may mutate it.

types.name: git_indexer_progress
types._comment_agent: git_indexer_progress is a public POD counter block with no pointer slots: six unsigned int counters plus a size_t received_bytes. Callers own the storage (stack or embedded) and pass it by pointer; git_indexer_append and git_indexer_commit assert it non-null, read and write its fields transiently, and never retain the pointer. The git_indexer_progress_cb callback receives it as const for the duration of one call only. It has no constructor, disposer or cloner; all-zero is the valid initial value.

types.name: git_iterator
types._comment_agent: git_iterator is an opaque public note-iterator alias with uniquely owned allocation. Internally, start/end are optional duplicated ranges owned by the iterator; cb and comparison callbacks borrow static function tables/functions; repo and index are optional mutable borrowed dependencies that must remain alive while variants use them.

Optional git__strdup range endpoint owned by the iterator and released by git_iterator_free.
Static case-sensitive or case-insensitive index-entry search function selected during initialization.
Optional borrowed index retained by index/workdir variants and used when releasing snapshots; git_iterator_free does not release the index itself.
Static prefix comparison function selected during initialization.
Optional borrowed repository used by tree/workdir variants; the iterator does not release it, and libgit2 operations may mutate repository internals.
Optional git__strdup range start owned by the iterator and released by git_iterator_free.
Static string comparison function selected during initialization.
Static bounded string comparison function selected during initialization.

types.name: git_mailmap
types._comment_agent: git_mailmap is an opaque heap allocation published by include/git2/mailmap.h and defined in src/libgit2/mailmap.h. Its single field is a by-value git_vector of owned git_mailmap_entry pointers; it holds no pointer slot of its own. git_mailmap_new allocates it, git_mailmap_free is its sole destructor (null-tolerant; frees every entry, disposes the vector, then frees the header), and there is no cloner. Every constructor copies its inputs: git_mailmap_add_entry duplicates the four strings, git_mailmap_from_buffer parses a counted borrowed buffer into copies, and git_mailmap_from_repository reads the workdir file, blob and config file into copies. A completed mailmap therefore borrows nothing and outlives the repository and buffers it was built from. Strings returned by git_mailmap_resolve are owned by the mailmap and live as long as it does.

types.name: git_merge_analysis_t
types._comment_agent: git_merge_analysis_t is a public unsigned-int bit set, not a closed enumeration: git_merge_analysis_for_ref clears the out-slot to GIT_MERGE_ANALYSIS_NONE (0) and then ORs in NORMAL (1), UP_TO_DATE (2), FASTFORWARD (4) and UNBORN (8), producing genuine combinations such as FASTFORWARD|UNBORN and FASTFORWARD|NORMAL. NONE is the empty set and is never returned on success. It is a scalar with no fields, storage or lifecycle, and travels only through caller-owned out-parameters that C writes and never retains.

types.name: git_merge_file_favor_t

It is not a bit set. It is a scalar with no fields, storage or lifecycle, and appears only as a by-value field of git_merge_file_options.favor and git_merge_options.file_favor, which callers own and libgit2 only reads.

types.name: git_oid
types._comment_agent: git_oid is a public by-value struct with no pointer members: a one-byte git_oid_t discriminator plus an inline GIT_OID_MAX_SIZE (32) unsigned char digest array. types.name: git_oid_t

types.name: git_oidarray

types.name: git_packbuilder

Reviewed against pack-objects.c: git__calloc zero-initializes every slot, so odb is absent until git_repository_odb succeeds and git_packbuilder_free guards it, and the two mutex-guarded counters carry their lock binding.

types.name: git_patch
types._comment_agent: git_patch is a refcounted polymorphic base. The public down-reference is git_patch_free; a per-instance static free_fn selects the concrete generated or parsed destructor when the count reaches zero.

ptr.note: Runtime-conditional: parsed patches allocate and free the delta, generated-from-diff patches borrow a delta kept alive by their retained diff, and direct generated patches point into their own derived allocation. Every fully formed public patch has a delta.

types.name: git_pathspec
types._comment_agent: git_pathspec owns its optional detached prefix string and is reference counted through rc. git_pathspec_new creates the first count; match lists increment it; git_pathspec_free releases one count.

types.name: git_pathspec_match_list
types._comment_agent: A match list owns one reference to its compiled pathspec, its matches pointer-array allocation, its failures array, and its pool. Match elements are borrowed: strings live in the list pool, while diff deltas live in the source diff.

ptr.note: Owned growable allocation of borrowed pointers. String-mode elements point into this list's pool; diff-mode elements point into the source git_diff and require that external object to remain alive.
Owns one refcount acquired by pathspec_match_alloc and released by pathspec_match_free; valid completed match lists always store a non-null pathspec.

types.name: git_proxy_options

Nullable function pointer; code storage is static and callback state is carried separately in payload.

types.name: git_push
types._comment_agent: git_push is opaque in the public API and handed to transport callbacks as a borrow. Its internal remote/repository pointers are borrowed; pb is temporary owned state whose stale field value must not be exposed.

types.name: git_remote_head
types._comment_agent: git_remote_head is a by-value advertised-reference record whose oid fields and local flag are inline; it has no destructor of its own, so the concrete owner (git_pkt_ref via git_pkt_free, the local transport's free_head, or a remote's reference vector) releases the record together with its strings. types.name: git_remote_redirect_t
types._comment_agent: Reviewed against include/git2/remote.h and src/libgit2/remote.c. The enumeration publishes exactly three values (NONE=1, INITIAL=2, ALL=4), and http.c switches on a single one rather than testing bits, so it is not a bit set. A follow_redirects field carries a fourth state: GIT_FETCH_OPTIONS_INIT and its siblings leave it 0, and remote.c's lookup_redirect_config reads 0 as unspecified, resolving it from http.followRedirects and falling back to INITIAL when the repository has no such setting or there is no repository. A wrapper must therefore model the field as an optional enum with 0 = unspecified, and must not default it to INITIAL.

types.name: git_repository
types._comment_agent: The public API exposes git_repository only as an opaque, uniquely owned allocation released by git_repository_free. Internally the repository owns one reference to each lazily populated database/config/index pointer, owns all cache and graft allocations, owns its duplicated path/identity strings, and owns the reserved-name array. Every pointer member is nullable during lazy initialization or for repositories without the corresponding path/cache, except reserved_names.ptr, which repository_alloc initializes before publishing a complete repository. Re-reviewed: the nullability of gitdir and commondir is observable through the public getters git_repository_path and git_repository_commondir, both of which return NULL for a repository built by git_repository_new, so their wrappers must be optional.

types.name: git_reset_t
types._comment_agent: Reviewed against include/git2/reset.h and src/libgit2/reset.c. Closed domain of SOFT=1, MIXED=2, HARD=3; git_reset switches on the value and rejects anything else with GIT_ERROR_INVALID, so 0 is not a valid value and the type has no default.

types.name: git_revert_options

types.name: git_signature
types._comment_agent: A fully initialized public git_signature owns non-null NUL-terminated name and email allocations. git_signature_free releases both strings and the header; git_signature_dup deep-copies the complete value. Public documentation also permits manual teardown of the three allocations.

types.name: git_smart_subtransport
types._comment_agent: All three vtable slots are installed from static functions before each concrete subtransport is published. They are required for a fully constructed object; action and close borrow the object synchronously, while free is its one final release.

ptr.note: A fully constructed subtransport stores a required, immutable code pointer installed from a static function; every implementation assigns it before publishing the object. The callback synchronously borrows its arguments. Its stream out-pointer is separately handled by the wrapper because stateful continuations may return an existing stream while RPC actions return new storage.
A fully constructed subtransport stores a required, immutable code pointer installed from a static function and invokes it synchronously with a borrowed self pointer.
A fully constructed subtransport stores a required, immutable static destructor callback. The callback consumes the concrete allocation reached through the embedded interface header.

types.name: git_smart_subtransport_definition
types._comment_agent: The definition is a borrowed by-value callback configuration with no lifecycle operation. callback and param are a coupled callable/state pair; rpc is a scalar behavior flag.

ptr.note: Required function pointer copied into the definition; every valid in-tree definition installs a static callback and git_transport_smart invokes it synchronously.

Optional type-erased caller state passed to callback. The custom callback stores its referent in the returned subtransport, which later mutates it, so its lifetime may extend through the resulting transport rather than only the synchronous factory call.

types.name: git_smart_subtransport_stream
types._comment_agent: A stream is a polymorphic header embedded at offset zero in a concrete allocation. `read` and `free` are required static code pointers; `write` is NOT - libgit2's own HTTP subtransport leaves it null for the two reference-advertisement (GET) services, so a safe wrapper must treat the slot as optional rather than assume it. The stream borrows its owning subtransport, which outlives it, while ownership of the concrete stream allocation is released through the installed free callback.

ptr.note: Required static concrete destructor callback; installed by every observed constructor. git_smart__reset_stream (smart.c:57) invokes it exactly once for the current stream and clears the slot, and it always runs before git_smart__free releases the originating subtransport (smart.c:426).

Required static synchronous callback. Installed on every path of every observed stream constructor, including both http.c service methods (http.c:707 and http.c:710); smart.c:29 calls it without a null check.

Every published stream constructor stores the originating subtransport (git.c:165, http.c:704, ssh_exec.c:100, ssh_libssh2.c:225, winhttp.c:1546, tests/libgit2/transport/register.c:148). The stream never frees it; read/write callbacks may mutate it through OWNING_SUBTRANSPORT, and smart-transport teardown frees the stream before the subtransport.

OPTIONAL static synchronous callback, corrected from the earlier 'required' judgement. http.c's http_action installs it only for the POST services (http.c:706-711): a stream created for GIT_SERVICE_UPLOADPACK_LS or GIT_SERVICE_RECEIVEPACK_LS is calloc'd and left with a null write slot. That is safe in C because the smart transport writes only to streams obtained for GIT_SERVICE_UPLOADPACK (smart.c:322) or GIT_SERVICE_RECEIVEPACK (git_smart__get_push_stream), plus the non-RPC goodbye flush in git_smart__close (smart.c:395), and never to an advertisement stream. Every other constructor (git.c:167, ssh_exec.c:102, ssh_libssh2.c:227, winhttp.c:1548, register.c:150) does install it, so nullability is a property of the concrete subtransport and the requested service, not of the struct.

types.name: git_status_options
types._comment_agent: git_status_options is a non-owning configuration header. Its optional baseline aliases a caller-owned tree. git_status_list_new reads the tree during construction, never mutates it, and deliberately does not free it when supplied by the caller.

types.name: git_strarray
types._comment_agent: git_strarray is a by-value header. Library output owns its counted pointer array and strings and is reset by git_strarray_dispose; input instances commonly borrow stack arrays and string storage and must not be disposed. Borrowed handles therefore only view contents, while owned CVal instances arise empty or from libgit2 output/deep copy.

ptr.note: Counted char-pointer array. Library-produced results own the outer allocation and each non-null NUL-terminated string; caller-supplied input arrays borrow both, so ownership is runtime-conditional. Null outer pointers represent empty arrays (malformed caller inputs may pair null with nonzero count), and git_strarray_copy explicitly tolerates null elements.

types.name: git_submodule
types._comment_agent: git_submodule is an opaque public refcounted handle. Its private layout owns name, url, and branch strings; path is either an alias of name or a distinct owned string. repo is a non-owning pointer to the parent repository, which must remain alive while repository-dependent submodule operations run.

Optional duplicated URL string; documentation explicitly permits NULL and submodule_release frees it.

types.name: git_submodule_update_options
types._comment_agent: git_submodule_update_options is a by-value, non-owning options header. Its checkout and fetch subrecords borrow any configured strings, objects, and callback state for the outer options lifetime; version and allow_fetch are plain scalars.

types.name: git_tag
types._comment_agent: The public type is opaque. Internal parsing allocates and initializes its three pointer fields; git_tag__free releases each before the tag storage.

types.name: git_time
types._comment_agent: git_time is a plain by-value timestamp: no pointer fields, no allocation of its own and no lifecycle primitive. The only aggregate that embeds it is git_signature.when, whose lifecycle releases it, so a borrowed handle projected out of the enclosing signature is the whole ownership story. `sign` is NOT a validated discriminator: git_signature__parse memsets the signature, so it stays 0 whenever the parsed buffer carries no timezone field, and src/libgit2/signature.c:389 copies tz_start[0] verbatim after the malformed-timezone branch has already reset offset to 0, so any byte can reach it. git_signature__writebuf reads it loosely, as '-' when the offset is negative or the byte is '-' and '+' otherwise. A Rust accessor must therefore validate the byte rather than transmute it, and treat 0 and stray bytes as ordinary, expected inputs.

types.name: git_transaction
types._comment_agent: The public API keeps transactions opaque. Reference transactions borrow their repository, own one refdb count, and keep lock/pool state inline; config transactions borrow the config and own the type-erased backend-instance count released indirectly by git_config_unlock. The variant discriminator makes the inactive pointer fields null.

Borrowed repository for the reference-transaction variant; the caller must keep it alive. Null for config transactions.
